Q: Azure Data Factory throwing "Invoking Azure function failed with HttpStatusCode - InternalServerError." A:

Call to provided Azure function 'OnCopySuccess' failed with status-'InternalServerError' and message - 'Invoking Azure function failed with HttpStatusCode - InternalServerError.

Has nothing to do with Azure DataFactory, it fails because of the Azure Functions, HAs from the error you will not be able to detect any issues so, you may examine the output of your azure function app using logs in kudu, in addition to the monitor of the azure function.

In addition, kudu log files are more timely than the Azure function's monitor. Simply navigate to this website's address. Click on the URL https://yourfunctionappname.scm.azurewebsites.net/DebugConsole

Go To: LogFiles\Application\Functions\Function\yourtriggername

The log files can then be found. The log file in Kudu is real-time, whereas the monitor takes a while to show (typically 5 minutes).

HTTP Function is supposed to actually return an HTTP result, See the Original Post - So you might check your Azure Function Code.

Q: Find current Windows BCD Store file path A:

You can use the bcdedit tool. You may export the BCD before making edits, somewhat along the following lines:

bcdedit /export oldbcd
cp oldbcd newbcd
bcdedit /store newbcd /delete <identifier>
bcdedit /import newbcd /clean

If you wish to see the current BCD entries to get that identifier:

bcdedit /enum firmware

Q: React Native error: requiring unknown module A:

According to the React-Native Docs there are a couple of ways to specify where your images come from:

Local Storage:

<Image source={require('./img/favicon.png')}/>

Network:

<Image source={{uri: 'http://facebook.github.io/react/img/logo_og.png'}}/>

Dynamic strings e.g. rowData.thumbnail can only be used for packaged images. See this issue.

If your images are loaded into images.xcassets on iOS and res/drawable on Android you can reference them by the filename like so:

<Image source={{uri:'thumbnailFileName'}}/>

or..

<Image source={{uri:rowData.thumbnail}}/>

You can also specify placeholders in the same way..

<Image source={{uri:rowData.thumbnail}} defaultSource={{uri:'placeholder'}}/>

Working demo - https://rnplay.org/apps/tsiGfQ

Q: Get latest partnership when start date is in one table & end date in another of partnerships A:

I'm starting to understand. However it is difficult to work with images of table schemas. Could you please:

  1. Reduce the schemas down to the minimum needed to work the problem.
  2. Post the reduced table schemas as text that includes column names and data types.
  3. Explicitly define what the relationships are between the tables.
  4. Looking at your tables, I am not clear to me what defines which couples are participating in which competitions and genres. Please explain.

For example, the competitors table might only need the ID, Name, and Male flag. Competition might only need the ID, Name, and Date. MaleID and FemaleID are both foreign keys that reference the Competitor table. And so on.

My partial understanding so far, is that:

  1. You wish to summarize the uninterrupted competition series for the latest active couples for each genre (Ballroom, Latin, Rhythm, Smooth).
  2. A given couple and genre is considered latest if neither partner has competed later in the same genre with a different partner.
  3. The uninterrupted competition series includes competitions back in time to the point where one or both partners competed in the same genre with a different partner.

If my understanding is incorrect or incomplete, please describe the required logic.

My initial thoughts were that this might be a gaps and islands problem for defining continuous partnerships. However, if we are only interested in the latest active couples, I think we could write logic that finds the latest series per participant per genre and then pair them up.

I can expand on this once I get more information as requested above.

Q: How to search and replace text in a file A:

You can totally do this natively on Windows with a quick PowerShell script. Just open your terminal and run something like this to loop through your folder and swap the text:

PowerShell

Get-ChildItem -Filter *.txt -Recurve | ForEach-Object {
    (Get-Content $_.FullName) | ForEach-Object { $_ -replace 'old string', 'new string' } | Set-Content $_.FullName
}

This works fine for basic text files, but it gets pretty tedious if you are dealing with complex regular expressions or working across a bunch of different file types.

I actually got tired of writing scripts for this, so I built a lightweight, portable Windows utility that handles mass updates across 30 different file formats without needing an install. It does literal swaps, advanced RegEx matching, and copies your originals to a backup folder so you don't accidentally wreck your data. If you want to check out the specifications or grab a copy, I keep the link right on my profile bio.

Q: gcc gfortran compiler does not recognize blank spaces inside filenames A:

I'll assume for now you're using something like Linux and bash. This should also work for Windows and MacOS to some degree.

The shell splits up the command into arguments and presents them to the program as parameters to main(int argcv, char * argv[]). Each argument separated by a space goes to a separate entry in argv[]. You can tell the shell not to use a space to split things up two ways.

First, precede it by a \ - the shell will ignore that space and remove the \ character. Second, put "" marks around the path that includes the space.

If I'm guessing wrong and your problem is actually something else, let me know.
